body:
**Price check**
- Google Finance: ₹200.50 at 19 Nov, 3:30 pm IST (−1.27%).
- Screener: ₹200.55 close on 19 Nov.
- The two agree. Upstox showed ₹166 on 2 Nov and Kotak ₹162.5 on 30 Oct. The stock re-rated about 30% after the Q2 results and peaked at about ₹218 on 12 Nov. The 52-week range is ₹99–220.
- Recomputed: TTM PAT of ₹182 cr over about 26.2 cr shares (FV ₹1 after the 1:10 split) gives EPS of about ₹6.95 and a **reported P/E of 28.9**. Google shows 29.8, while Screener's 23.5 P/E does not reconcile with reported numbers.
- **Adjusted:** add back the ₹49 cr Q4 FY26 exceptional (a Right-of-Recompense settlement) and remove the roughly ₹13 cr post-tax US customs refund in Q2. That gives TTM PAT of about ₹218 cr and a **P/E of about 24**. Market cap is about **₹5,250 cr**. The company has zero debt and ran a buyback.

**Annual figures (₹ cr, standalone)**
| FY | Sales | OPM | PAT | ROCE | Borrowings | CFO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY22 | 1,010 | 23% | 132 | 31% | 223 | 59 |
| FY23 | 1,179 | 22% | 198 | 32% | 82 | 213 |
| FY24 | 1,222 | 21% | 156 | 28% | 18 | 221 |
| FY25 | 1,155 | 21% | 174 | 23% | 14 | 227 |
| FY26 | 1,144 | 20% | 141* | 21% | 0 | 190 |
| TTM | 1,274 | 22% | 182* | – | 0 | – |

\* Reported figures, after the ₹49 cr exceptional. Over five years, CFO is ₹910 cr against PAT of ₹801 cr.

**Quarterly figures (₹ cr)**
| Quarter | Dec-24 | Mar-25 | Jun-25 | Sep-25 | Dec-25 | Mar-26 | Jun-26 | Sep-26 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | 260 | 284 | 292 | 271 | 275 | 306 | 304 | 389 |
| YoY | −5% | −10% | −6% | −10% | +6% | +8% | +4% | **+43%** |
| OPM | 20% | 18% | 21% | 20% | 21% | 18% | 23% | 24%† |
| PAT | 20 | 55 | 49 | 44 | 48 | **−0** (exceptional) | 60 | 74† |

† Includes about ₹18 cr of US customs refund. **Underlying Q2 OPM is about 21%** (management's figure).
- **There is a loss quarter inside FY26.** The Mar-26 quarter was a ₹0.15 cr net loss after the exceptional item.
- Sales were flat for eight quarters, and only one quarter shows the jump. That is **a single explosive quarter, not yet a sustained step-change.**

**Shareholding**
| Holder | Dec-24 | Sep-26 | Direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Promoter | 53.35% | 54.24% | Up, buyback effect |
| FII | 8.09% | 6.44% | Bounced from 5.40% in Jun-26 |
| **DII** | 31.62% | 25.74% | **Steady selling** |

Pledge was not independently verified.

**What drives the story**
- US tariff relief (50% → 18% or less) unlocked held-back demand. US component revenue more than doubled YoY.
- **Auto-component exports grew 89% YoY.** FY27 auto-component revenue guidance is ₹550–575 cr.
- Exports are 51% of component sales. A China+1 shift by global bearing and automotive Tier-1 suppliers is also at work.
- Bearing rings, the core business, grew only 6%.
- Freight is about 3x normal and is not passed through. Management guides FY27 OPM of 21–22%, with expansion in FY28 as freight eases.

body:
`insight:buffett-mistakes-admitted-2008-2025` | confidence: verified | date: 2026-02-28

Primary-source error log. 2008 letter: 'I made at least one major mistake of commission' - buying 'a large amount of ConocoPhillips stock when oil and gas prices were near their peak' ('the terrible timing of my purchase has cost Berkshire several billion dollars'); $244m in two Irish banks that 'appeared cheap', written down to $27m (-89%) by year-end ('unforced errors'); and errors of omission, 'sucking my thumb when new facts came in.' 2014: Tesco - 'I made a big mistake with this investment by dawdling'; after souring on management in 2013 he sold slowly; 'bad news often surfaces serially: You see a cockroach in your kitchen; as the days go by, you meet his relatives' (after-tax loss ~$444m per the letter). 1999: Dexter Shoe (bought 1993 with Berkshire stock) collapsed as ~93% of US shoes came from imports. 2024: 'During the 2019-23 period, I have used the words "mistake" or "error" 16 times'; 'The cardinal sin is delaying the correction of mistakes or what Charlie Munger called "thumb-sucking."' 2025 (Greg Abel): 'Our investment in Kraft Heinz has been disappointing ... our return has been well short of adequate'; Pilot - control delayed until 2023 by contract: 'That mistake will not happen again.' Patterns: buying commodity exposure near cyclical peaks; 'cheap' leveraged banks; slow exit when management or moat deteriorates; paying with own stock for a business whose moat is eroding. Actionable: write a sell trigger at purchase; act on the first cockroach.

Sources:
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/2008ltr.pdf
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/2014ltr.pdf
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/1999htm.html
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/2024ltr.pdf
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/2025ltr.pdf

- **Headcount** `[10K25 human capital]`: ~7,800 full-time and 16,800 part-time crew (FY24: 7,300 / 15,900). About 600 corporate, ~1,000 at ship centres and **~23,000 in stores** (FY24 21,500). That is **~12.0 crew per store in both years** (23,000/1,921; 21,500/1,771). Each store has a manager plus 1–2 assistant managers. District managers cover 10–15 stores. There is **no union**.
- **Payroll is not disclosed** as a line in the 10-K (the US GAAP gap vs India's employee-benefit note). [EST]: SG&A ex-D&A $1,065M − advertising 76 − SBC 35 − corporate payroll ~80 − other corporate ~150 → store payroll ~$650–800M = **13.6–16.8% of sales**, ~$340–420k per store. Cross-check: at ~$15.5/hour average plus a 15% load ($17.8), that is 19–24k hours per store per year (370–455 hours a week ≈ 9–11 FTE). It fits ~12 crew, most of them part-time. Two routes agree.
- **Sensitivity:**
  - 1% on the store wage rate ≈ $7–8M ≈ **15 bps of sales**.
  - A $1/hour step across all store hours ≈ $42–53M ≈ **90–110 bps** [EST: 36.5–46M hours × $1 × 1.15].
  - On the Q2 call, management "leveraged labor costs year over year" but had "invested more labor in the stores" since 2025 `[CC-Q2FY26]`.
- **The US difference from India:** most US value retailers already pay *above* the statutory minimum in most states. So the binding variable is the **local market wage** (BLS OEWS cashiers / retail salespersons by metro), not the statutory notification. Statutory steps matter where they bind: CA, NY, NJ, WA, IL, MA, MD, and FL's scheduled path to $15 (Sep-2026). [Schedule from memory, unverified. Verify on the DOL state minimum-wage table or the EPI tracker.]
- **Open item:** store count by state. The 10-K map is an image, so no text is extractable. Scrape the store locator, then build state count × (2026–27 legislated step) × hours → bps.

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:US-PNC:q4-2026-nii-4250m-plus`
- **Method:** sector cycle/lead indicator · **P(ours)** 0.60 · **P(base)** 0.55 · resolve by 2027-01-31
- **Evidence:** Q3 2026 financial highlights (Oct-2026): NII $4,206m (+2% QoQ, +15% YoY incl. FirstBank), NIM 2.94%; Q2 2026 NII $4,107m, Q3 2025 $3,648m; 'commercial loan growth and higher yields on interest-earning assets, partially offset by increased funding costs'; efficiency ratio 57%; Q4 buybacks to approximate Q3. US 10-yr yield Q4-to-date average 5.07% vs 4.75% in Q3 (Yahoo ^TNX).
- **Why our number differs from base:** Lead indicator: higher long rates keep lifting yields on PNC's repricing fixed-rate securities and loans (a multi-year tailwind the bank has cited), while loan growth continues; funding costs are the offset. $4,250m is only +1% QoQ, below the recent QoQ pace, so we lean slightly above the base.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Naive: NII rose QoQ in each of the last two reported quarters; a ≥1% QoQ rise in the next quarter has roughly 55% odds for a large regional bank.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if PNC's reported total net interest income (GAAP, not fully taxable-equivalent) for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 is ≥$4,250m per its Q4 2026 earnings release.
- **Resolution source:** PNC Q4 2026 financial highlights / earnings release (8-K, EDGAR)
- **Sources used:** https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/713676/000162828026065936/q32026financialhighlightsa.htm; https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/%5ETNX
- **Confidence of evidence:** single-source

title: CLAUDE › What this project is

body:
- 6 calls Q2-2025..Q3-2026: 5 Motley Fool transcripts plus the Q2-2026 8-K Ex 99.1 'Business Outlook' section (no Fool transcript found). Call dates from the transcripts' DATE lines (Monday after-close calls), not the fool.com publication dates.
- Ledger built by hand (fetch.py reads NSE, not US sources): Motley Fool takeaway list + targeted greps of the full text (guidance, outlook, organic, adjusted operating margin, EPS, free cash flow / conversion, capex, savings, price/cost). Quotes marked [Fool summary] are the transcriber's takeaway wording, not management's words. Pipeline v1.3 adds the US measure vocabulary to `score.py` for future runs.
- Restatements are folded into the first promise (`later_restatements`), not double-counted; a cut >= 2 quarters before the deadline is 'withdrawn' (clarification A).
- Outcomes: company-adjusted KPIs (organic growth, adjusted operating margin, adjusted EPS, segment margins) from the company's own later calls/releases (single-source); GAAP revenue, operating income, EPS, capex, FCF, buybacks and dividends re-derived from SEC XBRL companyfacts (`tools/sec_fetch.py facts`) as the second source.
- Scoring: pilot formula unchanged (`scripts_TD_peers/build_seed.py`; T&D clarifications A-D apply). Credit delivered 1 / partly 0.5; MCS weights specificity x materiality x recency.
